Article Title: How Jantar Mantar became Delhi's designated protest site and what changes now
Article Text:
Jantar Mantar’s changing role in Delhi’s history of dissent

Jantar Mantar’s legacy: A landmark site of dissent faces a shift

Before Jantar Mantar, there was Boat Club

When Rajpath became a protest ground

How Jantar Mantar became Delhi's protest address

When the right to protest reached the Supreme Court

What changes now?

Why the location of a protest matters

NEW DELHI: Jantar Mantar, one of Delhi's best-known protest venues, has lost its status as a designated site for demonstrations. On October 12, Delhi Police de-notified the site and named three alternatives: Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi.The decision follows recommendations from a committee constituted by the ministry of home affairs (MHA) to examine alternative venues for protests and demonstrations.For several decades, Jantar Mantar has been synonymous with protests in the national capital, a place where farmers, students, workers and political organisations have gathered to raise their demands.However, Delhi's address for protests has not always been Jantar Mantar. Before it emerged as a prominent hub for demonstrations, the sprawling lawns around India Gate and the Boat Club, close to Parliament and the government's principal offices, were among the capital's most important spaces for political mobilisation.The latest decision marks another chapter in the history of how authorities have regulated where citizens can assemble to make their voices heard.For decades after Independence, the Boat Club lawns near India Gate were an important venue for political rallies.The lawns near modern-day Central Vista gave demonstrators proximity to Parliament, the government's principal offices and other institutions at the centre of national power.The scale of the gatherings, however, also presented challenges for the authorities.One of the defining episodes came in 1988, when farmer leader Mahendra Singh Tikait led a massive agitation in Delhi. Farmers gathered at the Boat Club and surrounding lawns to press their demands, bringing a large mobilisation into the heart of the capital.The episode became a turning point in the debate over whether such prominent public spaces should remain open to large demonstrations.Authorities increasingly sought to regulate gatherings in central Delhi, citing concerns around security, traffic and public order.In 'India After Gandhi: The History of the World's Largest Democracy', historian Ramachandra Guha recounts how the lawns along present-day Kartavya Path, formerly Rajpath and known as Kingsway during British rule, became a prominent site of political dissent in the early 1990s.The book recalls tents occupied by people from different parts of the country, representing causes ranging from demands for a separate state and better prices for agricultural produce to recognition for regional languages.Other groups included industrial workers, Tibetan refugees seeking Indian citizenship and Hindu religious organisations campaigning on cow slaughter.The lawns near the country's most prominent government buildings in Lutyens' Delhi became a temporary home for movements that wanted their demands to be seen and heard.But the encampments did not last. Guha writes that the tents were dismantled in the early 1990s, with the government concerned about the impression created by visible demonstrations near the ceremonial heart of the capital.Protesters subsequently regrouped near Jantar Mantar, where they remained visible to people passing through the busy commercial district.The restrictions on gatherings around Boat Club and Rajpath helped set the stage for Jantar Mantar's emergence as a prominent location for demonstrations.Built by Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II in the 18th century, Delhi's Jantar Mantar is an open-air astronomical observatory designed to track celestial movements.Over time, the area around the historic site evolved into a major hub for protest movements, offering demonstrators a prominent public platform while remaining easier to manage than larger, more central locations.Located close to busy Connaught Place and within reach of Parliament and government offices, it allowed demonstrators to bring their demands into public view without occupying the expansive lawns around India Gate.The site hosted protests involving workers, farmers, civil society groups and citizens campaigning on a range of social and political issues.Its prominence grew further during the anti-corruption movement led by social activist Anna Hazare in 2011, when demonstrations demanding a stronger Lokpal mechanism brought corruption and accountability to the centre of national political debate.As the movement grew, Ramlila Maidan became the venue for larger gatherings and Hazare's prolonged fast. The two locations demonstrated how different sites in Delhi could accommodate protests of different scales.The significance of Jantar Mantar was not simply a matter of geography. It became an established public address for people seeking to draw the attention of political leaders, government officials and the media to their grievances.Over the years, Jantar Mantar has witnessed protests on a range of issues, from Anna Hazare's campaign for a Lokpal Bill and the 2017 Tamil Nadu farmers' agitation to demonstrations against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act and the wrestlers' protests against Brij Bhushan Sharan Singh in 2023.More recently, it became the centre of demonstrations by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) over the NEET paper leak and demands for the resignation of then Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan.However, its status as a designated protest venue did not mean that demonstrations could take place without restrictions. Police permissions, public-order measures and court directions continued to determine how the site could be used.In October 2017, the National Green Tribunal (NGT) ordered an end to protests at Jantar Mantar following complaints about noise, sanitation and disruption to residents.The restrictions were subsequently challenged before the Supreme Court.In its July 23, 2018, judgment in Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan v Union of India, the Supreme Court examined restrictions on protests at Jantar Mantar and the Boat Club, including the effects of demonstrations on residents and public spaces.The court recognised peaceful assembly and protest as fundamental rights under Articles 19(1)(a) and 19(1)(b) of the Constitution. At the same time, it acknowledged that the exercise of these rights could be regulated to protect public order and the interests of other citizens.The judgment addressed the competing claims of demonstrators and residents, making clear that one group's rights could not simply extinguish those of another.It called for a balance between the right to protest and the need to prevent unreasonable disruption.The constitutional basis for that balance is set out in Article 19. Article 19(1)(b) guarantees citizens the right to assemble peacefully and without arms, while Article 19(3) permits reasonable restrictions in the interests of the sovereignty and integrity of India or public order.The latest decision comes amid protests by opposition parties and the youth-led CJP against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.The proposed CJP protest on October 10 was met with extensive security arrangements, detentions and restrictions on movement in parts of Delhi.Under the new arrangement, Jantar Mantar will no longer be a designated protest venue. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi have been identified as alternatives.Delhi Police has said a detailed and revised standard operating procedure for demonstrations at these three venues will be issued separately.The decision changes where organisers can hold demonstrations under the designated-venue system. However, de-notification should not be confused with a blanket prohibition on all peaceful assembly, which remains subject to constitutional protections and lawful restrictions.The significance of the decision extends beyond the physical relocation of demonstrations. The location of a protest affects its visibility, the ease with which people can reach it and its proximity to the institutions being addressed.A venue in central Delhi offers demonstrators a different kind of access and public visibility from a ground farther away from the corridors of power.For organisers, the choice of location can therefore be an important part of how a protest communicates its message.Among the newly designated venues, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi are farther from the central government district than Jantar Mantar.At the same time, large demonstrations in central Delhi can create challenges for traffic management, security and the daily movement of residents.The October 10 protests, for instance, were accompanied by extensive security arrangements and disruptions to movement across parts of the city.The latest decision once again brings into focus a question that has shaped Delhi's protest history for decades: how to balance the right to peaceful demonstrations with security, public order and the functioning of the national capital.
Article Summary: Delhi Police de-notified Jantar Mantar on October 12. Ramlila Ground, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in East Delhi have been named as alternatives. The decision follows recommendations from a committee constituted by the ministry of home affairs.

Article Title: LeT conspiracy case: NIA attaches Srinagar property used to shelter 2 Pakistani terrorists

NEW DELHI: The National Investigation Agency (NIA) on Monday attached a residential property in Srinagar Jammu and Kashmir , belonging to an accused in a case linked to a cross-border terrorist conspiracy involving the proscribed Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) outfit.The property, owned by Ghulam Mohammad Mir alias Mama Gas, is located in Danihama village in Srinagar’s Hazratbal area. The NIA attached it under Section 25 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.According to the anti-terror agency, its investigation established a direct link between the property and the terrorist conspiracy.“The premises were used for harbouring Pakistani terrorists and concealing incriminating material connected with the terror network. Investigation exposed a network of local Over Ground Workers (OGWs) working in coordination with LeT handlers to facilitate the infiltration, movement, shelter and logistical support of Pakistani terrorists for carrying out attacks against government establishments, security forces and civilians,” the statement read.The NIA also revealed that a search conducted at Mir’s residence on April 6 led to the detection of two Pakistani terrorists, identified as Abu Huraira and Khubaib, who were associated with the LeT.An explosive-like substance, digital devices and other incriminating material were also recovered and seized from the premises.The investigation further indicated that “the accused had knowingly provided his residential premises as a haven for the terrorists and had allowed the property to be used for facilitating their activities,” the agency noted.The NIA is continuing its probe to identify and expose the wider terror-support network, including other OGWs, facilitators and individuals linked to the Pakistan-based handlers.The case was initially registered at Zakoora Police Station in Srinagar on March 31, 2026, before being taken over and re-registered by the NIA.
Article Summary: The property, owned by Ghulam Mohammad Mir alias Mama Gas, is located in Danihama village in Srinagar’s Hazratbal area. The NIA attached it under Section 25 of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act, 1967.

Article Title: 'Anyone can join Shiv ki Baraat': Rahul Gandhi likens CEC protest to Lord Shiva's Tandav; BJP hits back
Article Text:
Rahul Gandhi, Shivaraj Singh Chouhan

BJP attacks Congress over Lord Shiva reference

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi on Monday likened the ongoing protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to “Lord Shiva’s Tandav”, saying the movement did not require a fixed plan and that anyone willing to join the fight to protect the Constitution was welcome.The remarks drew a sharp response from Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, who accused the Congress of having no connection with the country’s traditions and faith. “They do not even have the right to invoke the name of Lord Shiva,” he said.Speaking at a press conference at the All India Congress Committee (AICC) headquarters ahead of the INDIA bloc’s planned march to the Supreme Court, Gandhi said the protest would continue in different forms, depending on the circumstances.“My sister tells me that we should make a plan. So I told my sister, 'You are not understanding the point. This is Tandav. This is Lord Shiva’s dance. There is no planning in this. Today we are going to the Supreme Court; tomorrow it will be something else. What do you think? Did we make a plan at Akashvani Bhavan?“The plan was that we would go by bus, sit there, and get arrested. The police wouldn't let us go. So we changed the plan.Did the result come from the plan, or did it come from the non-plan? There is no need for any plan. This dance is ongoing. This is Lord Shiva’s dance going on. In this, anyone can join Shiva's procession (Shiv ki Baraat). Anyone who wants to join, can come,” he said.Gandhi said the demonstrations were aimed at questioning the conduct of the Election Commission and demanding Kumar’s resignation. He claimed that people across the country were raising questions about the chief election commissioner and warned that the agitation would continue.“Why is all this happening? Because we are only asking the question raised by two Election Commissioners: why is Gyanesh Kumar not resigning? These days, we are receiving information from everywhere. Gyanesh Kumar, we know your situation. We know you are unable to sleep at night, and do not worry, we will not spare you. I am telling you directly that you will not escape as Election Commissioner because of what is happening. Lakhs of people are questioning you and your conduct, and they will not stop,” he said.The Congress leader also alleged that questions were being raised within security agencies over the treatment of protesters compared with members of the Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS)."Questions are being raised within the police about why they are being asked to stop the youth while RSS members are being allowed to roam freely. These questions are being raised within the Home Ministry, Delhi Police, CRPF and ITBP,” he said.Gandhi urged people from all political parties to join the INDIA bloc’s march at 1.30 pm from Barakhamba Junction in Connaught Place, describing it as a movement to protect the Constitution. He also appealed to those unable to participate directly to express solidarity when the delegation reached the Supreme Court to file its petition."India is marching; join us today at 1.30 PM at Barakhamba Junction in Connaught Place. If you want to protect the Constitution, anyone from any party can join...If you cannot join us directly for any reason, show your solidarity when we will be in front of the Supreme Court filing the petition,” he said.Responding to Gandhi’s remarks, Chouhan accused the Congress of invoking religious symbolism despite, according to him, being disconnected from India’s cultural traditions."Look, I have said this before as well: they have nothing to do with the country’s values, traditions or faith. They do not even have the right to invoke the name of Lord Shiva," Chouhan said.The Union minister also dismissed the Opposition’s protests as an expression of frustration over repeated electoral defeats and accused the Congress of blaming constitutional institutions for its political setbacks."The reason for Congress's defeat is not the Election Commission; the reason for Congress's defeat is Congress's own idea-less leadership. What is the current state of the Congress? There is infighting in Uttar Pradesh. In Punjab, they have had to change the state president. In different places, there are conflicts over leadership. In Karnataka, sometimes it's Siddaramaiah, sometimes it's D.K. Shivakumar. In Telangana, there is internal conflict.Chouhan further accused the Congress of undermining constitutional institutions and cited its record of dismissing elected governments."What will they talk about the Constitution? They have sinned by changing elected governments more than 90 times," he said.The INDIA bloc’s planned march comes amid Opposition allegations of electoral irregularities and demands for Kumar’s resignation. The delegation intends to approach the Supreme Court with a petition raising concerns over the Election Commission and the conduct of elections.Security was tightened across central Delhi ahead of the march, with police barricades and deployments of Delhi Police, the Rapid Action Force and the Central Reserve Police Force. Entry and exit at several metro stations were also scheduled to remain closed until 4 pm for security reasons.
Article Summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi likens ongoing protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar to "Lord Shiva's Tandav" Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan accused the Congress of having no connection with the country's traditions and faith. Gandhi urged people from all political parties to join the march at 1.30 pm from Barakhamba Junction in Connaught Place.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has permitted a delegation of 10-15 people from Congress party to go to the filing counter inside the premises as Rahul Gandhi leads INDIA bloc's march to the top court.However, the delegation would be outside the high-security zone to file their petition, sources told TOI.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi began his planned march to the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar.The Congress MP called for the "Challo Dilli" protest march, which was planned from Connaught Place to the Supreme Court against the functioning of the poll body.The opposition continued the protest despite the CJI not giving his assent to a meeting with the opposition MPs on the issue.Earlier in the day, Rahul Gandhi also called for a news conference on the protest. In a post on X he said, "March for Democracy. March for Justice. Chalo Dilli."Chief Justice of India (CJI) Justice Surya Kant, however, on Monday said every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court and that the Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone, amid the INDIA bloc's planned protest march to the court against the Election Commission.Responding to the INDIA bloc's request for a meeting, the CJI said he had received a letter on Sunday and replied to it the same night, explaining why he would not be able to meet the delegation."I received a letter yesterday regarding a meeting request, and I responded to it last night, outlining the reasons why I will be unable to meet," CJI Surya Kant told reporters after NHRC's 33rd Foundation Day function.He also emphasised that any citizen or elected representative could approach the court and seek legal relief."The Supreme Court's doors are open to everyone. Any petition from any common citizen or member of an elected body is welcome. Every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court, and we will hear their concerns and grant whatever is due under the law," he said.CJI Justice Surya Kant had earlier rejected the INDIA bloc leaders’ request for a meeting to submit a representation over alleged electoral irregularities, stating that they should approach the court by filing a petition as the matter is already sub judice.
Article Summary: 10-15 people from Congress party to go to the filing counter inside the premises as Rahul Gandhi leads INDIA bloc's march to the top court. The delegation would be outside the high-security zone to file their petition. Chief Justice of India Justice Surya Kant said every Indian citizen has the right to approach the court.

Article Title: 'Don't pick up words like this': SC says neither approved nor disapproved new Form 6, to examine its validity
Article Text:
The revised declaration has come under scrutiny over changes introduced by the Election Commission.

What is Form 6 controversy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday stated that it had neither approved nor disapproved the new Form 6 declaration used for voter registration, saying it had not adjudicated on its validity and would examine the issue.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana made the oral observations while hearing a writ petition concerning the functioning of the Election Commission of India (EC) and changes to voter registration forms.Form 6 is the application through which an eligible person seeks inclusion in the electoral roll.During the hearing, advocate Narendra Mishra, appearing for the petitioner, referred to the Election Commission's claim that the Supreme Court had approved the new Form 6 declaration."There is no adjudication on the new Form 6," Justice Bagchi said, clarifying that the court had only observed that the new form was not in existence when it delivered its judgment on the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls in Bihar in May 2026."What the Hon'ble Chief Justice said was that when the Bihar SIR judgment was delivered, new Form 6 was not there. That does not either say it is approved or disapproved by the Supreme Court.We will examine it," Justice Bagchi said, according to LiveLaw.The Chief Justice cautioned lawyers against reading too much into the court's observations, saying, "Don't pick up words like this ..."The bench agreed to issue notice on the petition and listed the matter for October 27 along with connected petitions concerning Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.The new Form 6 declaration has become controversial following allegations that changes were introduced into the voter registration process without following the prescribed legal procedure.Under the revised declaration, applicants seeking registration as new voters are required to state whether they or their parents were mapped in the previous SIR. The earlier Form 6 used during electoral roll revisions in other states did not seek such a declaration.The controversy intensified after The Indian Express reported that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected to the changes, arguing that the form could not be modified without an amendment to the Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, by the Central government.On September 26, the Election Commission issued a press release suggesting that the Supreme Court had upheld the new Form 6 declaration in its May 2026 judgment concerning the Bihar SIR.However, the Supreme Court clarified on October 5 that it had not approved modifications to Form 6.
Article Summary: Supreme Court says it has not adjudicated on the validity of the new Form 6 declaration. The new declaration has come under scrutiny over changes introduced by the Election Commission. The Chief Justice cautioned lawyers against reading too much into the court's observations, saying, "Don't pick up words like this..."

Article Title: Why CJI declined to meet Rahul Gandhi, Kharge amid protests against Gyanesh Kumar
Article Text:
CJI Suryakant, Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant had declined a request from Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge for a meeting to discuss issues arising from the ongoing protests in Delhi.He said the matters are already pending before the Supreme Court and discussing them administratively would violate the principle of separation of powers.In a letter dated October 11, the CJI advised the two Opposition leaders to approach the Supreme Court through the judicial process instead of submitting a memorandum on the administrative side. He also assured them that any petition filed on the issues would be heard at the earliest possible opportunity in accordance with the law.The request concerned allegations of irregularities involving the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and the Election Commission of India, alleged arbitrary arrests of students, the closure of metro stations and the cancellation of trains amid protests in the national capital.Explaining his decision, CJI Surya Kant said the issues raised by Gandhi and Kharge were “already sub judice before the Supreme Court of India .”“Therefore, convening a meeting to discuss pending cases would wholly contravene the principle of Separation of Powers, an intrinsic facet of the basic structure doctrine of the Constitution of India, and would be incompatible with the established ethics and judicial propriety,” the CJI said.He also clarified that the Supreme Court did not have administrative powers to address the concerns raised in their letter, but could examine them through its judicial jurisdiction.“However, in the exercise of our jurisdiction under Article 32 of our Constitution, along with other plenary powers, including that of judicial review, we are duty-bound to consider on the judicial side the gravamen of issues affecting the citizens of India,” he said.The CJI reiterated the Supreme Court’s commitment to protecting citizens’ fundamental rights and said they could seek their enforcement through the legal process.“Supreme Court of India reiterates its commitment to preserve and protect the Fundamental Rights of every citizen of India and they are entitled to seek enforcement of such rights at all hours through the procedure known in law. It would thus be more appropriate on your part to invoke the judicial powers of the Supreme Court of India, instead of submitting a memorandum on the administrative side,” he said.Pointing to the court’s schedule, CJI Surya Kant said matters involving similar issues were listed for hearing on Tuesday, October 13, 2026. He invited the Opposition leaders to file a petition on Monday, either physically or through the court’s e-filing facility.“If so advised, you may submit your petition on Monday, either physically at the Supreme Court of India, between 10:30 A.M. and 04:30 P.M., or alternatively, by utilising the e-filing option, which permits filing at any time and on any day. You have my assurance that any such petition shall be heard at the earliest possible opportunity, in accordance with the law,” he said.Gandhi and Kharge had sought an appointment with the CJI amid Opposition protests demanding the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of electoral irregularities, including what Congress has described as “vote chori”.Kharge said in a social media post on Sunday that the Opposition would continue its fight and that he and Gandhi had written to the CJI seeking a meeting.“We will continue our fight. Tomorrow, we are also going to meet CJI. I have written a letter, and Rahul Gandhi has also written a letter. We have scheduled a meeting between 4-5pm, during which we will apprise him of the situation... Chaos is being created in the country by home minister and PM, and everywhere an undeclared emergency is imposed,” Kharge said.The CJI’s response leaves the Opposition leaders free to pursue their concerns through a formal petition, with the court indicating that related matters could be taken up through judicial proceedings.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant declined a request from Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge for a meeting. He said the matters are already pending before the Supreme Court and discussing them administratively would violate the principle of separation of powers. Gandhi and Kharge had sought an appointment with the CJI amid Opposition protests.

Article Title: 'Singhasan khali karo': Shashi Tharoor's poetic post as Congress ups ante against CEC
Article Text:
Shashi Tharoor shared a poetic post to back the protest against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.

Jantantra Ka Janm"

Singhasan khali karo ki janata aati hai

NEW DELHI: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has backed Rahul Gandhi 's call for the ouster of the current BJP government and the poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar. Tharoor shared an excerpt from Ramdhari Singh Dinkar's popular poem, "(The Birth of Democracy).(Vacate the throne, for the people are coming!)," Tharoor shared in a post. Interestingly, these lines long echoed India's political corridors during the JP movement against the national Emergency imposed by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in 1975.Tharoor called it the poem of the day, coinciding with Rahul Gandhi's planned march to the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, who has been under fire from the opposition over his handling of the contentious Special Intensive Revision (SIR).“This government will go,” Tharoor also said in a previous post.In a show of opposition unity, a large demonstration led by INDIA bloc leaders and lawmakers wound its way through the streets of the national capital before reaching the Constitution Club of India.Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress general secretary Priyanka Gandhi Vadra and party chief Mallikarjun Kharge, along with former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee , arrived at the Constitution Club.Rahul Gandhi had called on citizens to join the INDIA bloc's protest march towards the Supreme Court against alleged "vote theft".He said the alliance was moving to file a petition following directions from the Chief Justice of India (CJI).In a post on X with the hashtag #ChaloDilli, the Congress leader urged people to gather at Connaught Place in central Delhi to participate in the demonstration, which aims to safeguard democratic and constitutional values."We had written a letter to the CJI. He directed us to file a petition. Now, leaders of the INDIA alliance will march to the SupremeCourt against 'vote theft' and file the petition," Rahul Gandhi posted on X.Appealing for nationwide participation, he urged citizens to join the march in person or raise their voices from wherever they were."In this fight to protect democracy and the Constitution, fellow citizens, let us march step in step with us. Reach Connaught Place and become part of this march. If you can't come, raise your voice from wherever you are! #ChaloDilli," the LoP added.During the march, Congress general secretary (organisation) KC Venugopal launched a sharp attack on the central government, describing the opposition's agitation as the 'biggest andolan" against the poll panel and announcing that the party was taking its legal battle to the Supreme Court.'This is the biggest andolan against the Election Commissioner and the election system. Narendra Modi and Amit Shah are using the Chief Election Commissioner as their tool to destroy the democracy of this country, to hijack the democracy of the country," Venugopal said.
Article Summary: Senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor has backed Rahul Gandhi's call for the ouster of the current BJP government and the poll body chief Gyanesh Kumar. He shared an excerpt from Ramdhari Singh Dinkar's popular poem, "(The Birth of Democracy).(Vacate the throne, for the people are coming!)" The lines echoed India's political corridors during the JP movement against the national Emergency imposed by then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi in 1975.

Article Title: SC restored people's faith: Kapil Sibal a day after venting frustration
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court 's order Sunday finding prima facie breach of its Oct 9 order against complete shutdown of Metro and train services and issuing notice to Union home secretary, Delhi Police commissioner and Delhi Metro chief altered over the course of a day senior advocate and Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal 's views on the apex court.On Saturday, Sibal had told reporters "if we go to courts, I do not know whether we will ever get relief. The people of this country have decided that this govt has to go. If anyone can save the Constitution at this juncture, it is Supreme Court."He added, "I am tired of repeatedly approaching the SC. It's in my mind that there is no purpose in going there. I have not much expectations from SC. Whatever is to happen will happen. I only pray the country's democracy remains intact... The tribunals (in West Bengal) have allowed appeals of 93% voters whose names were deleted illegally. SC has come to know this. But we did not get any relief".On Sunday, he was leading a 100-strong team of lawyers in SC to question the detentions of protesters and alleged violations of court's Oct 9 order against shutdown of Metro and rail services. The emotionally charged arguments saw pro-protester lawyers paint a picture of injustice and violation of fundamental rights on Saturday, compare it to an "undeclared emergency" and shout down a senior advocate who said lawyers must confine their activities to courts and not hit the streets, and that freedom of speech came with reasonable restrictions.At an appropriate juncture, Justice Joymalya Bagchi said, "Our purpose is to instil people's faith in the system, and in that process your (lawyer's) confidence is most vital for our fight against injustice." The court also passed a slew of directives, including normalising Metro, train and internet services and traffic in the city and allowing lawyers and journalists to carry out professional work.Soon after the SC order, Sibal said, "We are deeply grateful to the Supreme Court for passing an order that restores the faith of the Indian people, as well as the faith of professionals, in the justice system of this country."Within an hour of SC passing the order, a senior advocate entered into an argument with cops over removal of barricades, citing the SC ruling. The order was yet to be made public and police personnel didn't know about it.
Article Summary: Supreme Court's order Sunday finding prima facie breach of its Oct 9 order against complete shutdown of Metro and train services. Rajya Sabha MP Kapil Sibal's views on the apex court altered over the course of a day. Sibal had told reporters "if we go to courts, I do not know whether we will ever get relief"

Article Title: North Korea fires multiple ballistic missiles towards S Korea, Seoul urges Pyongyang to stop ‘UN violations’
Article Text:
North Korea fires missiles towards sea, escalating tensions on Korean Peninsula (Reuters image)

North Korea fired multiple ballistic missiles towards its eastern waters on Monday, South Korea’s military said, as Pyongyang continued its weapons testing amid heightened tensions and a prolonged freeze in diplomatic engagement.South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were launched from an area near the North Korean capital, Pyongyang. Japan’s Defence Ministry detected at least two missiles and assessed that they had landed in waters outside the country’s exclusive economic zone.South Korea’s presidential office condemned the repeated launches, saying they violated United Nations Security Council resolutions and urging Pyongyang to stop such activities immediately.The latest launches came days after South Korea flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon on Friday. Designed to travel at least five times the speed of sound and evade missile defence systems, the weapon was described by President Lee Jae Myung as an important step towards strengthening the country’s conventional defence capabilities.North Korea has intensified its weapons development as leader Kim Jong Un seeks to expand the country’s arsenal of nuclear-capable systems.On October 3, Pyongyang conducted a test of what it described as a hypersonic intermediate-range missile designed to penetrate missile defence systems in South Korea and Japan.The country has also carried out missile tests and live-fire drills and commissioned a new warship, underscoring Kim’s push to strengthen its military capabilities despite repeated US and South Korean offers to resume diplomatic engagement.Tensions on the Korean Peninsula have also been aggravated by a series of land mine explosions near the heavily militarised inter-Korean border last month that injured three South Korean soldiers. South Korea’s military and the US-led United Nations Command concluded that the blasts were caused by mines planted by North Korea. Pyongyang has denied responsibility and dismissed Seoul’s demands for an apology.Kim has halted diplomatic engagement and cooperation with South Korea in recent years, describing the neighbouring country as a permanent enemy. Nuclear negotiations with Washington have also remained stalled since 2019, when talks broke down during US President Donald Trump’s first term.Kim has so far rejected Trump’s overtures to revive dialogue. Pyongyang has demanded that Washington abandon what it calls its “hostile” policy and drop denuclearisation demands as a precondition for negotiations.The impasse has complicated Lee’s efforts to pursue engagement with North Korea. While advocating dialogue and adopting a more conciliatory tone, the South Korean president has also called for stronger conventional defence capabilities and reduced reliance on the United States.Washington unilaterally scaled back a major military exercise with South Korea in August, with Trump citing his “very good relationship” with Kim.
Article Summary: South Korea’s Joint Chiefs of Staff said the missiles were launched from an area near the North Korean capital, Pyongyang. Japan's Defence Ministry detected at least two missiles and assessed that they had landed in waters outside the country's exclusive economic zone. The latest launches came days after South Korea flight-tested its first domestically developed hypersonic weapon.

Article Title: How India travels: A tale of two wheels and many divides
Article Text:
File image of urban traffic

India on the move

Rural-urban divide

Two Indias, Two Ways to Travel

Students take the bus, workers take the bike

Men ride, women walk

The Gender Divide in India’s Commute

Short commutes, steeper city bills

The work clock

For long trips, the bus still rules

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A quarter-century ago, an advertising campaign presented the two-wheeler as a symbol of “Naye Bharat ki Nayi Tasveer”. But is the India of 2026 still commuting mainly on two-wheelers, has it moved to cars, or are more people walking? The answer depends a great deal on which states people live in, whether they are in a village or a city, and on their gender. All three, in varying degrees, shape how people get around and how much they pay for it.Among some of the extremes featured in India’s National Household Travel Survey, in Puducherry, 92.7% of workers use a two-wheeler as their primary mode. In Nagaland, more than seven in ten walk. West Bengal has the highest published bicycle share, Ladakh stands out for buses, and Sikkim for cars. Conducted from July 2025 to June 2026, the survey covered 4,92,023 households and 18,44,179 people aged six and above.At the national level, the old two-wheeler image still rings true, though the averages hide big regional differences. Among workers who travel at least 1km to work, 42.6% mainly use a two-wheeler, 28.3% walk and 10.7% cycle. The average one-way trip to a fixed workplace takes 25 minutes, and travel costs about ₹785 a month per worker.Between India and Bharat, the numbers shift substantially. In rural India, workers are split almost evenly between two-wheelers at 37.1% and walking at 36.6%.In cities, the balance tips firmly towards the engine, presumably because of longer distances. Two-wheelers rise to 52.3% and walking falls to 13.5%. Autos, buses and cars all carry a bigger share too.The metro and local-train story is overwhelmingly urban. The survey’s Train/Monorail/Tram category, which includes metro rail and suburban or local trains, carries 5% of urban workers but just 0.4% of rural ones. In urban Maharashtra, home to Mumbai’s suburban railway, the share is 20.7%. It is 16.5% in urban West Bengal and 14.4% in Delhi, known for its metro network.The survey reports Rail separately. That category accounts for just 0.2% of workers nationally, 0.2% in rural India and 0.3% in urban India.Students and workers commute very differently. In villages, 40.5% of students walk and 18.9% cycle. In cities, buses at 33.7% and autos at 14.4% play a bigger role. Nationally, 37% of students walk, 29.5% take a bus and 15.8% cycle, while only 6.7% use a two-wheeler. Among workers, buses account for just 6.7%, exactly the share two-wheelers have among students.The contrast is sharpest in Kerala, where buses carry 72% of students but 24.9% of workers. Age changes the picture too. Students aged 15 to 29 walk far less than those aged 6 to 14, 22.2% against 47.3%, and cycle more, 21.4% against 11.9%.Among workers, 47.1% of men use a two-wheeler to get to work. Among women, it is 18.4%. About half of female workers, 50.6%, walk, against 24.1% of men. Women are also much more likely to take the bus, 14% against 5.3%.It would be easy to put this down to rural India, where more people walk. But the divide holds in cities too. There, 57% of male workers use two-wheelers, against 25.8% of women, while women are twice as likely as men to walk, 24% against 11.6%. The bicycle divide is even starker in relative terms. Among workers, 12.3% of men cycle to work but only 1.7% of women do.Yet among students, the sexes are much closer. Some 17.7% of male students cycle, against 13.4% of female students. Odisha makes the contrast particularly striking. Female students there cycle almost as often as male students, 32.8% against 34%. Among workers, though, the Odisha gap opens up. Some 25.5% of men cycle to work, against 5.8% of women.Most work commutes are under half an hour. Some 83.4% of workers travelling to a fixed workplace get there within 30 minutes. Students do even better, with 87.6% reaching school or college within half an hour.However, travelling in cities is much costlier. The average urban trip to work takes 27 minutes, just four more than in villages, but costs ₹1,044 a month against ₹612, about 71% more. Urban students pay about 71% more too, even though their average trip is a shade shorter, 22 minutes against 23 in villages.Even within cities, there are stark differences. Workers in urban West Bengal and urban Delhi spend about the same time getting to work, 36 and 35 minutes on average. But the urban West Bengal worker spends about ₹825 a month, while the urban Delhi worker spends about ₹2,081, roughly two and a half times as much.Urban West Bengal also has a much bigger long-commute tail. Some 13% need over an hour to commute, against 4.1% across urban India. Hence, lower monthly spending there does not necessarily mean a quicker journey.Across India, 56.5% leave for work between 8am and 10am. In Mizoram and Ladakh, some 97.1% and 95.1% of commuters leave between 8am and 10am.Evenings vary even more. Across India, 31.1% leave work at 6pm or later. In Tamil Nadu it is nearly half, 48.9%, with Gujarat at 45.2% and Delhi at 44.6%. Men are more than twice as likely as women to be leaving that late, 34.1% against 16%.Take work and study out of the picture and far fewer people step out at all. On a given day, 18.7% of people aged six and above travelled at least 1km for some other reason, 23.8% of males and 13.3% of females.They also get there differently. Among men making such trips, 40.1% use a two-wheeler, against 17.6% of women. Among women, 30.4% take an auto or e-rickshaw, against 12.7% of men. For women, autos and e-rickshaws play much the same role that two-wheelers do for men.In the 28 travel days before the survey, 11.3% of households made an overnight trip of 50km or more that kept a member away from home for more than 24 hours. More than half of these households, 55.8%, used the bus as their primary mode.The separately reported Rail category comes next at 17.7%. Cars account for 15.1% and two-wheelers 8.8%. Another 3.3% fall under Train/Monorail/Tram. Just 0.6% travelled by air.Few of these trips were about work. Some 70.2% of households making overnight trips travelled for socialising, communication or religious purposes.How far are people travelling? The answer is not provided in the details released so far. The survey collected trip distances, as well as information on licences, household vehicles and bus or rail passes, but none of these appears in the released estimate tables.A quarter-century after the “Naya Bharat” pitch, the two-wheeler still leads the national picture. But the survey shows how much that picture hides, and the big missing piece is how far India travels. At a time when there is demand for metros in every Tier 2 city and road and rail connectivity is better than ever, the full data, when released, will help policymakers make more informed decisions about how to prioritise India’s transport needs.
Article Summary: In Puducherry, 92.7% of workers use a two-wheeler as their primary mode. In Nagaland, more than seven in ten walk. West Bengal has the highest published bicycle share. Ladakh stands out for buses, and Sikkim for cars.

Article Title: 'Your confidence is most vital': Supreme Court to Kapil Sibal after his 'no faith' remark
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Sunday said its purpose was to instill faith of the people in the system and addressed Kapil Sibal 's "no faith" remark, saying his "confidence is most vital" for the top court's "fight against injustice".“Our purpose is to instill faith of the people in the system and in that process your (Sibal’s) confidence is most vital for our fight against injustice,” the bench said.The Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to prevent illegal detention of people participating in peaceful gatherings amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. It also asked the Centre to ensure that metro services operate normally and internet access remains uninterrupted, subject to law and order requirements.Sibal welcomed the court's order in connection with the restrictions imposed in Delhi amid protests, saying it restores faith in the country's justice system.“We are deeply grateful to the Supreme Court for having passed an order that restores faith among professionals in the system of justice in this country,” Sibal said.A bench comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued notice to the Centre while hearing a petition seeking contempt proceedings over alleged violations of the court's earlier order against a "complete prohibition" on metro and train services in the national capital during the protests.The CJP and several student organisations had called for demonstrations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the functioning of the Election Commission.The authorities prevented a planned mass mobilisation at Jantar Mantar on Saturday following a major security clampdown. More than 7,000 protesters were detained, including CJP leader Abhijit Dipke, several opposition leaders and YouTuber Dhruv Rathee.During the special hearing, the bench asked Solicitor General Tushar Mehta to ensure that Delhi Metro operates according to its regular schedule and that internet services are not disrupted, subject to law and order requirements.The court also directed authorities to ensure that lawyers, journalists and others are not prevented from carrying out their professional duties."Internet facilities shall remain undisturbed, as per law....When we are saying internet facilities shall remain undisturbed, we are not taking away the powers under the Information Technology Act."There shall not be illegal detention, save and except by procedure established by law, particularly with regard to assemblage of people beyond the area within which it's imposed," the bench said.The Supreme Court also directed authorities to remove a notice board outside its premises announcing the imposition of Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), which empowers authorities to restrict assemblies in certain circumstances."We have been informed that a notice board stating imposition of Section 163 BNSS in and around the vicinity of the Supreme Court has been put up."We direct the authority concerned to take down this board, if not already done, so that citizens as well as lawyers can have access to justice," the bench ordered.During the hearing, senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Rashtriya Janata Dal (RJD) MP Manoj Jha, alleged that police were detaining people travelling on trains and those found outside the four-kilometre radius of Jantar Mantar, where prohibitory orders were in force.Sibal also told the court that 45 metro stations had remained closed to passenger entry and exit despite the Supreme Court's October 9 order.The petition sought contempt proceedings against the authorities over the alleged failure to comply with the court's directions on maintaining access to public transport during the protests.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court on Sunday directed authorities to prevent illegal detention of people participating in peaceful gatherings amid the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) protests in Delhi. It also asked the Centre to ensure that metro services operate normally and internet access remains uninterrupted, subject to law and order requirements.

Article Title: Don't detain peaceful protesters, says SC; hundreds still taken away on Day 2
Article Text:
Normalise internet connectivity, ensure free movement in city: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Sunday sought responses of Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi police commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi metro rail chief D Thara to a contempt petition for prima facie violating the court's Oct 9 order against complete shutdown of metro and train services in Delhi on Saturday to thwart CJP's protest seeking CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation. The court also said lawyers, journalists, and other professionals should not be hindered in performing their duties "in any manner whatsoever".On the ground, nearly 700 people were detained (police claimed 400), many far away from protest zones, while barricading and traffic curbs remained on the roads much like Saturday. Protesters changed strategy, staging flash protests in small numbers at short notice. Most of the action was in and around CP as small groups of protesters kept trickling in. They were detained.Around 2.30pm, All India Student Association members, including president Neha Bora, started a protest near RK Ashram Marg metro station. As detentions began, Bora and a few others broke away and ran towards CP, where they continued to protest before being detained. Around 7pm, Students Federation of India members gathered at CP to hold a women's tiranga march against alleged police excesses, especially against women protesters.They were detained and taken away in buses. "How can they detain women at 7pm in the evening?" SFI general secretary Srijan Bhattacharya said.The widespread detentions - 7,000 estimated Saturday - figured prominently in arguments by the lawyers at SC's unusual holiday hearing on Sunday. Following the submissions, a bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said, "...we are of the opinion that the petitioners have made out a prima facie case. Accordingly, we issue notice upon the alleged contemnors". It asked them to file their responses by Oct 13.We understand the gargantuan magnitude of detentions. We will have to seek a response from govt," the bench said after hearing the petitioners, who included advocate Shailendra Mani Tripathi, CPM MP M A Baby, RJD MP Manoj Jha and lawyer intervenors like Shadan Farasat, who was detained along with other advocates outside SC on Saturday.The bench asked for normalisation of internet connectivity and prohibition of "illegal" detentions, especially of those who gather for peaceful protest away from areas where prohibitory orders are in force. "There shall be no illegal detentions, particularly in cases of peaceful unarmed assemblage of people beyond the area where prohibitory orders under Sec 163 of BNS are in force," it said.On Oct 9, SC had restrained authorities from resorting to blanket closure of metro stations, though it said operations could be regulated depending on the situation. The order came after DMRC said 57 stations would be shut; that number was later revised to 45.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta disputed allegations of violation of the Oct 9 order and said Delhi Metro was functioning normally, though 45 out of 303 stations were closed to maintain law and order. He refuted the allegation that metro stations were closed, saying that "all metro stations are open since 10pm Saturday, trains are operating normally and internet connection has been restored".SC also issued directions to ensure free movement in the city subject to law and order situation/traffic regulations and that installing barricades shall be reviewed forthwith to ensure free movement subject to law and order and traffic requirements. "Lawyers, journalists and other professionals shall not be hindered in discharge of their professional duties in any manner whatsoever," SC said, and also directed withdrawal of prohibitory orders around SC and courts to facilitate free access to litigants and lawyers.Over 100 lawyers led by senior advocate and MP Kapil Sibal slammed the police brutalities on protesters, and accused authorities of continuing with the shutdown of metro and train services in complete disregard of the SC order and of illegal detention of protesters even in areas where the prohibitory orders were not in force.Sibal argued that internet shutdown was a blow to fundamental right to free speech and flagged detention of lawyers who participated in the protest. Senior advocate Farasat, who was detained, informed SC he was manhandled and bundled into a police vehicle. Senior advocate and TMC MP Menaka Guruswamy termed the entire episode as "undeclared emergency" worse than what Indira Gandhi had imposed (in 1975).When Sibal thanked the bench for holding court on Sunday because of the extraordinary turn of events, Justice Bagchi said, "We are always at the service of the nation." Later, Justice Bagchi said, "We know things have deeply affected you (the lawyers) and we do not want to trivialise anything."The bench issued notice to Centre and Delhi Police on a habeas corpus petition questioning detention of TMC politicians Mamata Banerjee, Derek O'Brien and Dola Sen. Solicitor general Mehta said the petition has become infructuous as the detained leaders were released last evening.As the pro-protest petitioners backed by a team of senior advocates - K K Venugopal, N Hariharan, Shoeb Alam, Arundhati Katju, G Sankaranarayanan, Sanjay Hegde - made a concerted attempt to corner police and Centre by flagging police action, senior advocate Kirti Uppal struck a discordant note by arguing that lawyers should not be stepping into shoes of their political affiliation."I was told that a lawyer's job is inside the courts and not on the streets," he said. The pro-protester lawyers inside the courtroom shouted 'shame, shame' to silence him. The bench asked the lawyers to maintain decorum of the courtroom and maintain silence.
Article Summary: Supreme Court seeks responses of Union home secretary Govind Mohan, Delhi police commissioner Anurag Kumar and Delhi metro rail chief D Thara. Nearly 700 people were detained (police claimed 400), many far away from protest zones, while barricading and traffic curbs remained on the roads. Protesters changed strategy, staging flash protests in small numbers at short notice.

Article Title: 'Next PM Vijay 2029’: Placards trigger brief stir at PM Modi event in Chennai

PM Modi and Vijay share stage at Chennai Metro inauguration

PM Modi vows to work with Vijay for Tamil Nadu's development

NEW DELHI: A brief stir broke out at an official government function attended by Prime Minister Narendra Modi in Chennai on Sunday after some people displayed placards projecting Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay as the “next PM”.The incident took place at the IIT Madras campus, where PM Modi was addressing a gathering after inaugurating and laying the foundation stone for projects worth around Rs 13,000 crore across Tamil Nadu.CM Vijay was also present at the event.During his speech, P Modi mentioned Vijay's name, prompting a group of people, apparently supporters of the chief minister, to whistle and display handwritten placards bearing Vijay's photographs and slogans, including “Next PM Vijay 2029”, according to news agency PTI.Police personnel deployed at the venue intervened and instructed the individuals to sit down and lower their placards.Although they complied initially, they continued displaying the placards after the police turned away, gesturing towards video cameras.The incident occurred during PM Modi's first visit to Tamil Nadu since the April Assembly elections, which brought Vijay's TVK to power.The prime minister and the chief minister shared the stage during the inauguration of several infrastructure projects.They also jointly flagged off a new Chennai Metro service and travelled on the train.PM Modi inaugurated the Poonamallee-Vadapalani stretch of Phase II of the Chennai Metro Rail Project, built at a cost of around Rs 4,900 crore. The new stretch covers approximately 15 km and has 11 elevated stations.The two leaders also jointly inaugurated other scheduled projects during the visit. Vijay received PM Modi on his arrival in Chennai and saw him off before his departure for Delhi.In his address, PM Modi said his commitment to Tamil Nadu's development would remain unchanged despite changes in government."Governments may change, but my resolve for Tamil Nadu's development, serving its people remains steadfast. With this determination to serve people, together with CM Vijay, we are taking forward the development of the state," he said.PM Modi also highlighted cooperative federalism, saying that the country's development depended on the progress of its states. He recalled his experience of working with several Tamil Nadu chief ministers during his political career.Vijay, meanwhile, said cooperation between the Union and state governments was essential to ensure that people benefited from development initiatives."When the union and state governments work together, its benefit should directly reflect in the lives of the people, and that is our approach," he said.The chief minister also sought the release of Rs 5,110 crore in outstanding central funds under the Samagra Shiksha Abhiyan scheme without conditions. He called for steps to make Tamil the principal language of the Madras High Court.Vijay also urged the Centre to approve Phase III of the Chennai Metro project, reconsider metro proposals for Coimbatore and Madurai, and consider an inter-state metro line linking Hosur in Tamil Nadu with Bommasandra near Bengaluru. He further sought high-speed rail corridors between Chennai and Kanyakumari and Chennai and Coimbatore.During the visit, PM Modi praised Tamil language and culture and referred to the ancient Tamil classic Thirukkural, describing it as a guide for life.He recalled gifting a Russian edition of the work to Russian President Vladimir Putin and cited its teachings on learning and putting knowledge into practice.PM Modi also paid tribute to national poet Mahakavi Bharati and referred to the continuing relevance of the poet's verse Achamillai, meaning “there is no fear”.The prime minister also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for highway projects, Amrit railway stations, port-related initiatives and the Group II/III Lube Oil Base Stocks project at the Chennai Petroleum Corporation Limited refinery in Manali.The visit included meetings and joint public appearances between PM Modi and Vijay as the two governments highlighted their cooperation on infrastructure and Tamil Nadu's development.
Article Summary: PM Modi vows to work with Vijay for Tamil Nadu's development. Incident occurred during PM Modi's first visit to Tamil Nadu since the April Assembly elections, which brought Vijay's TVK to power. Police personnel deployed at the venue intervened and instructed the individuals to sit down and lower their placards.

Article Title: BJP Mahila Morcha protests against Congress MP Akoijam over harassment allegations, burns Rahul Gandhi's effigy

NEW DELHI: BJP Mahila Morcha workers staged protests across the country on Monday, burning effigies of leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam over allegations of sexual harassment involving female students at Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU).The protesters demanded action against Akoijam, who represents Inner Manipur in the Lok Sabha, and accused the Congress leadership of remaining silent over the allegations.BJP workers also marched towards the Congress office in Delhi, calling for the MP's removal and arrest.The protests followed reports that JNU had dismissed Akoijam from his position as a professor after an internal committee found allegations made by 11 female students to be true, according to the BJP. The allegations have not been independently verified in the material provided.Sharing a video on X, the BJP criticised the Congress leadership over its response to the allegations. BJP leader and MP Bansuri Swaraj questioned Rahul Gandhi's silence and challenged the party to take action against Akoijam.She said, “On October 9, 2026, a report from JNU's internal committee emerges, in which the allegations of sexual exploitation made by 11 female students against Congress MP Angomcha Bimol Akoijam are found to be true, and he is immediately dismissed from his job.“I want to ask Rahul Gandhi ji and the Congress... why have you remained silent until now? “Why haven't you taken action yet?“Rahul Gandhi ji, is ‘Smash The Patriarchy’ just an electoral slogan for you? “If not, then take action against Bimol Akoijam.”Swaraj also contrasted the BJP's position on women's political representation with her criticism of the Congress.“On one side is PM Shri Narendra Modi, who is increasing women's political representation through 'Women's Reservation.' On the other side is Rahul Gandhi, who obstructs even its implementation, gives a place in the Lok Sabha to a Sexual Predator, and provides protection to him through his silence,” she added.In another post, BJP MP Kamaljeet Sehrawat called on Rahul Gandhi to respond to the allegations."Rahul Gandhi should answer to those daughters who had come to India's renowned university (JNU) with trust. Article Title: No more a free circus, but a tamasha worth crores

The protest launched by Congress and left-wing student unions in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has posed several serious questions before the country’s political culture and democratic system. Congress and left-wing organizations have demanded the immediate removal of Gyanesh Kumar from the post of Chief Election Commissioner.A petition regarding this had also been filed in the Supreme Court. This petition demanded the removal of Gyanesh Kumar from his post. Even after the Supreme Court dismissed this petition, Congress’ Yuvraj Rahul Gandhi, along with his party’s MPs, has been wreaking havoc on the streets of Delhi every single day.There is a popular saying in Maharashtra, “Bin Paishacha Tamasha”, which means a tamasha born out of sheer foolishness that costs not even a penny. This surely entertains the onlookers. But the tamasha of the protest staged by the Congress and left-wing organizations is not free of cost; instead, it is costing crores of rupees every day. Paid protesters are being brought in. Unmasking the mastermind behind this multi-crore drama deserves a separate article.There is a competition going on between Rahul Gandhi and left-wing student unions to prove who is better in expressing fierce opposition to the Modi government by taking to the streets. When the footage of a young woman representing left-wing organizations climbing over a barricade and pushing women police officers went viral on social media, Yuvraj Gandhi felt a sudden urge to show just how brave he was. He began to fear that his own TRP might drop when this young woman was systematically brought into the limelight by left-wing organizations.It was out of this fear that he staged a protest march to the Chief Election Commissioner's office and satisfied his urge by climbing over police barricades. No country in the world has ever seen an opposition leader so childish, shallow and terrified for his very existence. Rahul Gandhi has sworn to tarnish the reputation of the office of Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.He takes pride in bringing each and every Lok Sabha session to a standstill by creating a ruckus. Even though the Delhi Police have denied permission for the protest, Rahul Gandhi has become an expert at things like pushing down the police barricades and manhandling police officers. He is making a desperate attempt to prove himself as the Leader of the Opposition by acting like a Bollywood hero. He has destroyed his own reputation due to this frenzied behaviour.Rahul Gandhi does not have the intellectual capacity to understand that such cheap aggression does not help in politics. He should learn how to oppose a government from his grandmother Mrs. Indira Gandhi's life. The Janata Party government had appointed the Shah Commission to inquire into the atrocities committed during the Emergency.The Shah Commission found Indira Gandhi guilty. Subsequently, the police went to her home to arrest her. Mrs. Indira Gandhi surrendered to the police without any ruckus. But before that, she had called all the journalists and photographers in Delhi to her home. She calmly got herself arrested in front of them. She systematically gained the sympathy of voters through this. Now, that is what you call a shrewd politician.These days, Rahul Gandhi keeps on picking fights with the police over one thing or the other. His tactics, like marching towards the Prime Minister’s residence or attempting to enter the Election Commission’s office, show that he does not have even a basic understanding of politics. Even the common man has started to realise that Rahul Gandhi was just trying to get some publicity by trying to enter the Election Commission’s office without any prior appointment. Rahul Gandhi has decided to defy all parliamentary and government rules, conventions and laws.From a security perspective, security rules are extremely strict at places in Delhi such as Parliament House, Rashtrapati Bhavan, the Prime Minister’s residence etc. Rahul Gandhi must certainly be aware of the laws and rules, as he has been an MP for more than 22 years. Still, he is trying to break the law again and again. He is still not mature enough to understand that such gimmicks give temporary publicity, but do not make his leadership popular. In fact, it seems that he does not even want to develop such maturity.Not a single Congress leader currently has the courage to tell Rahul Gandhi, who has been criticizing the Special Intensive Revision (SIR), that the Congress won in Kerala after this exercise was carried out. Rahul Gandhi, who accuses the EVMs of being manipulated, deliberately ignores the fact that he himself won an election by a margin of more than six lakh votes which was conducted using these very EVMs. He also conveniently forgets that the BJP won a majority when election was conducted through EVMs in 2014, when his own party was in power.Yuvraj is even failing to understand that such behaviour is causing him to lose his standing among the people. He is so obsessed with publicity that he has even forgotten that he is fighting against Narendra Modi and the Bharatiya Janata Party. He thinks that he is in competition with the youth who are gaining publicity by protesting in Delhi. He is not even bothered that he is adding to the difficulties faced by ordinary people in the Delhi region by staging protests every now and then and blocking roads. These protests can, at most, make him a reel star for a few days. He won’t get anything beyond that. Of course, he does not have the intellectual capacity to understand this. Therefore, there is no doubt that he will be more provocative and dramatic in the coming days.
Article Summary: The protest launched by Congress and left-wing student unions in Delhi against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar has posed serious questions before the country’s political culture and democratic system. Rahul Gandhi has sworn to tarnish the reputation of the office of Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha. Unmasking the mastermind behind this multi-crore drama deserves a separate article.

Article Title: India’s agri-seed sector accounts for the largest share of receipts under benefit sharing regulations during April-Sept
Article Text:
ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation,

NEW DELHI: India’s agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts from users of the country’s biological resources during April-Sept period this financial year under the Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) regulation -- a statutory mechanism which ensures that when local genetic resources create commercial value, a fair share flows back to states and communities to sustain that diversity.Though the amount of little over Rs 7 crore for the sector during that six-month period is not much, the receipts, at least, reflect working of the ABS mechanism in generating money by getting payment for utilisation of a diverse range of biological resources across agriculture sector.The other sectors that generate receipts include food, pharmaceuticals, biotechnology, medicinal plants, microorganisms and livestock. A total of around Rs 9.6 crore was received by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) towards access to biological resources from users in various sectors during the period.Contributions were received by the NBA from both domestic and international entities, including companies from Sri Lanka, Germany, France, the Republic of Korea and Bhutan.Union environment ministry’s records show that the NBA has realised around Rs 278 crore through ABS and disbursed more than Rs 200 crore towards biodiversity conservation and benefits for communities, farmers, institutions and other benefit claimers across the country since 2008.The Authority, a statutory body under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, regulates access to India's biological resources and associated knowledge and implements the Nagoya Protocol’s (a global convention) principle of fair and equitable sharing of benefits.Biological resources, used by different entities for developing seeds, include livestock genetic resources such as Mithun, Jersey cattle and frozen semen of Murrah buffalo, as well as Red Sanders wood sourced from cultivated sources and auctioned material. The range further includes agricultural crops such as chickpea, red lentil, green moong, horse gram, flaxseed, guar gum, tapioca, buckwheat, brown rice, cauliflower, okra, hot pepper, brinjal and ridge gourd.The biological resources also include medicinal plants such as Ashwagandha, Shatavari, Kalmegh, Vasaka, Licorice, Arjuna, Bacopa, Gotukola and Moringa, as well as soil microorganisms including Azospirillum, Azotobacter, Bacillus, Rhizobium, Trichoderma and Metarhizium.The ABS mechanism goes beyond monetary collection by linking the utilisation of biological resources with biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and equitable sharing of benefits.“Funds disbursed through the State Biodiversity Boards and Union Territory Biodiversity Councils support conservation of biological resources, preparation and updation of People's Biodiversity Registers, strengthening of Biodiversity Management Committees, biodiversity research and documentation, and benefits to local communities and other benefit claimers,” said the Union environment ministry on working of the mechanism and utilisation of the collected money.ABS-funded activities can complement relevant govt schemes and programmes, particularly those promoting tribal welfare, sustainable livelihoods and natural-resource-based enterprises, such as the Pradhan Mantri Janjati Adivasi Nyaya Maha Abhiyan (PM-JANMAN), Pradhan Mantri Janjatiya Vikas Mission and Pradhan Mantri Van Dhan Yojana.“Such convergence can strengthen community-led conservation, sustainable utilisation of biological resources and livelihood opportunities, while leveraging existing institutional mechanisms,” said the ministry in a statement.India’s ABS framework supports Target 13 of the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework on the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from the utilisation of genetic resources and associated traditional knowledge, as well as Target 19 on resource mobilisation. The framework also contributes to relevant Sustainable Development Goals, including SDG 2 (Zero Hunger), SDG 8 (Decent Work and Economic Growth), SDG 12 (Responsible Consumption and Production), SDG 15 (Life on Land) and SDG 17 (Partnerships for the Goals), through biodiversity conservation, sustainable resource use, livelihood support and institutional collaboration.“As India prepares to participate in the seventeenth meeting of the Conference of the Parties to the Convention on Biological Diversity (COP 17), commencing on 19 October 2026 in Yerevan, Armenia, its ABS framework demonstrates the country’s continued commitment to biodiversity conservation, the sustainable use of biological resources and the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from their utilisation,” said the ministry.
Article Summary: The agri-seed sector accounted for the largest share of receipts from users of the country’s biological resources. A total of around Rs 9.6 crore was received by the National Biodiversity Authority (NBA) towards access to biological resources from users in various sectors.

Article Title: HC questions Assam government on woman sent to Bangladesh
Article Text:
Not only Mumtaz, another woman also 'missing' after B'desh expulsion

Gauhati high court has intensified scrutiny of circumstances in which Nagaon's Mumtaz Begum was sent to Bangladesh, warning Assam govt that it would presume a Foreigners' Tribunal's May 30 opinion declaring her a foreigner would be considered "not ready" if the state fails to establish when it was finalised.In its latest order on Oct 7, the high court recorded MEA's submission that an inquiry into Mumtaz's whereabouts was ongoing and that it needed more time.TOI had reported that Bangladesh's home ministry began searching for Mumtaz after this newspaper contacted authorities in Dhaka in the last week of Sept.The Gauhati high court, in its Oct 7 order, said, "The court shall presume that the opinion...was not made ready within the appropriate time, i.e., prior to the taking into custody" of Mumtaz.The court had ordered an inquiry on Sept 3 and directed MEA to trace Mumtaz and facilitate her return, observing that she was sent to Bangladesh without a "reasonable opportunity" to challenge the tribunal's opinion.The court had previously set aside an earlier opinion declaring her a foreigner and ordered fresh consideration of her case.Her son, Momruz Ali, had on Oct 7 disputed Assam CM Himanta Biswa Sarma's claim that she was safe and in regular contact with him and had told TOI that the family had no idea where she was and that the family was "breaking" under the strain of the search.The case dates back to April, when Gauhati HC set aside an earlier Foreigners' Tribunal opinion declaring Mumtaz a foreigner and remanded the matter for fresh consideration. She appeared before the tribunal again on May 30, the date borne by the fresh opinion, and was taken into custody.The central question now before the court is whether that opinion had actually been made ready before officials acted on it.According to the chronology recorded in court proceedings, Mumtaz was subsequently moved through holding facilities in Assam and handed over to BSF on June 13.BSF told the court she was "sent back to Bangladesh" in the early hours of June 14, from the Kalaincherra area of Cachar. Her whereabouts have remained unknown to her family since she was sent across the border, according to her son.Mumtaz is not the only woman from Nagaon reported missing after being sent across the border. Another woman, Jahanara Begum, whose case is ongoing in HC, has also gone missing under similar circumstances.The high court heard her case together with that of Mumtaz Begum.
Article Summary: Gauhati high court has intensified scrutiny of circumstances in which Nagaon's Mumtaz Begum was sent to Bangladesh. Court warns Assam govt that it would presume a Foreigners' Tribunal's May 30 opinion declaring her a foreigner would be considered "not ready" if the state fails to establish when it was finalised.
