NEW DELHI: The Congress and other opposition parties will march to the Supreme Court on Monday, October 12, demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protest comes a day after a police crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi and amid fresh political tensions over the alleged misuse of force against protesters.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi has called on young people, opposition parties and civil society groups to join the march. The Congress has named it "Chalo Delhi - March for Democracy" and said participants will assemble at 1.30pm at the Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road junction.The opposition plans to submit a memorandum to Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, demanding an end to alleged "vote chori", a halt to SIR and Kumar's resignation. However, sources said on Sunday night that the CJI had not agreed to meet Gandhi and Leader of Opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge, who had sought an appointment between 4pm and 5pm on Monday.Rahul, in a post on X, urged people to unite beyond party, gender, caste, community and state."Yesterday, the nation's young came out in Delhi to peacefully protest. They came with love in their hearts, not hatred or anger. They were beaten, both by cops and BJP goons. This is not the India we want," he said."Tomorrow, we will march to the Supreme Court as Indians, united beyond party, gender, caste, community and state. Youth, all opposition parties, civil society groups, all those who believe in democracy and stand by the Constitution of India, will walk with us," he added.The march follows Saturday's police action against protesters demanding Kumar's removal. Several demonstrators, including activists of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), were detained as security personnel prevented them from reaching the designated protest site.On Sunday, the Supreme Court directed authorities to immediately lift prohibitory orders under Section 163 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita around the apex court complex. A bench of Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said peaceful citizens should not face illegal detention and that movement across Delhi must be allowed in accordance with the law.The court was hearing petitions challenging the police crackdown and detentions, along with a contempt plea alleging disobedience of its orders.Meanwhile, CPI(M) Rajya Sabha MP John Brittas was taken to Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital after he was allegedly manhandled by police during Sunday's protest. He later sought an independent investigation and accountability from the President, the Rajya Sabha chairman and the CJI.Brittas alleged that police personnel dragged him for around 50 metres, forcibly put him in a vehicle and assaulted him inside it before leaving him by the roadside. Congress MP Shashi Tharoor condemned the alleged mistreatment and called for an investigation.CJP activists also vowed to continue their agitation after Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were released following their preventive detention."We will take to the streets again; we will not be intimidated by people like Amit Shah and Modi. Throw us in jail not just once, but a hundred times," Dipke said.Delhi Police DCP Neha Yadav defended the detentions, citing alleged law-and-order violations during previous demonstrations, including stone-pelting, arson and damage to public property. She said prohibitory orders had been imposed in several areas to maintain public safety.Opposition leaders, however, accused the government of suppressing dissent. RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav said "an Emergency has been declared", while Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav alleged that women protesters had been mistreated.The BJP dismissed the allegations and accused the opposition of creating chaos. Union minister Sukanta Majumdar said the opposition "occasionally makes its presence felt, much like a cockroach crawling across one's back."BJP leader Karuna Sagar also challenged Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders to follow the constitutional procedure for removing the CEC. He said any evidence of wrongdoing should be presented before Parliament.Union minister of state Tokhan Sahu defended the electoral roll revision process, saying it had taken place under successive governments. Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta also criticised the opposition protests and praised Delhi Police for maintaining public safety.The latest confrontation follows the opposition's earlier march from Parliament to Vijay Chowk, after which INDIA bloc leaders submitted a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu. The Congress and its allies are now seeking to take their demands to the Supreme Court as the dispute over electoral rolls and Kumar's position intensifies.
Article Summary: Congress and other opposition parties will march to the Supreme Court on Monday, October 12. They are demanding chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar's resignation over alleged irregularities in the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. The protest comes a day after a police crackdown on demonstrators in Delhi and amid fresh political tensions.

Article Title: Less-than-2-lane NH stretches shrink to 8% as high-speed corridors surge
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Barely 8% of the country’s 1.46 lakh km national highway (NH) network is now less than two lanes wide, compared with 2018-19, when such stretches accounted for nearly one-fourth of the network. Data shows the length of less-than-two-lane NHs has shrunk by 64% over the past nine years to around 13,000 km.In contrast, the length of high speed corridors (HSCs) has expanded more than 12-fold, while highways with four or more lanes have grown 1.5 times.Officials said the focus of highway development has increasingly shifted towards HSCs, greenfield access-controlled corridors and expressways. As these corridors are at least four lanes wide, their share in the overall NH network is expected to rise further. They said this would facilitate faster movement of passengers and freight while reducing logistics costs.However, despite the push for wider and seamless road connectivity, the average speed of trucks and the distance they cover each day remain well below global benchmarks. A truck in India typically covers only 300-350 km a day, compared with 700-800 km in the US and around 550-650 km in China.Officials said a comparison of truck speeds on two parallel highways illustrates the advantage of access-controlled corridors. On the Ahmedabad-Vadodara Expressway, trucks were found to travel at an average speed of around 80 kmph, compared with about 52 kmph on the parallel NH-64. The study also found that daily truck traffic on the expressway is nearly double that on the existing national highway.People aware of the govt’s plan to go for more HSCs said that the target is to build around 51,000 km of such network in the next 10 years, including the corridors developed or to be built by state govts.
Article Summary: Barely 8% of the country’s 1.46 lakh km national highway network is now less than two lanes wide. In 2018-19, such stretches accounted for nearly one-fourth of the network. Data shows the length of less-than-two-lane NHs has shrunk by 64% over the past nine years.

A vessel carrying 11 Indian seafarers came under a drone attack off the coast of Oman on Sunday, leaving two crew members missing while 9 were rescued, said minister of ports, shipping & waterways Sarbananda Sonowal."On Oct 11, tanker MT PETRO DOLPHIN, carrying 11 Indian seafarers, was subjected to a drone attack at Sohar Anchorage. While nine of our Indian crew members have been successfully rescued and are safe, two Indian nationals currently remain missing," said the minster."Search-and-rescue operations are actively underway by the local Coast Guard. We are continuously coordinating with all relevant authorities to fully support the ongoing rescue efforts and ensure every possible action is taken to safely locate our missing personnel," he added.Indians have been facing dangers in Middle East recently amid renewed tensions. On Saturday, 11 Indians were injured when Riyadh airport came under attack. A day later, the Indian embassy in Saudi Arabia announced that one of them had died.The Embassy of India in Riyadh said it had been following up on Saturday's attack and was in touch with local authorities and hospital officials to enquire about the condition of the injured Indians.Read more: One Indian killed, 10 injured in Riyadh airport strike; chilling video shows aftermath

NEW DELHI: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant has rejected the INDIA bloc leaders’ request for a meeting to submit a representation on alleged “vote chori”, ANI reported on Sunday. In an email response to the opposition leaders, the CJI explained the reasons for declining their request.In response to the request the CJI said that the apex court cannot interfere with the executive’s functioning on the administrative side, sources told news agency PTI. He asked the Congress leader to file a petition on the judicial side, which could be taken up on Tuesday. The CJI also said the Supreme Court was open 24x7 to citizens whose fundamental rights were violated, PTI reported.Leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi and Rajya Sabha LoP Mallikarjun Kharge had sought an appointment with the CJI between 4pm and 5pm on Monday to submit a memorandum demanding action over alleged electoral irregularities.Rahul had announced that opposition parties, civil society groups and young people would march to the Supreme Court, seeking Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar’s resignation, a halt to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and a return to paper ballots.The move to approach the CJI followed a meeting between INDIA bloc leaders and President Droupadi Murmu on Friday, during which the opposition submitted a memorandum outlining four demands.These included the CEC’s resignation, scrapping assembly elections held over the past two years, suspension of the SIR exercise and restoration of paper ballots. The memorandum also sought the restoration of 13.30 crore voters allegedly deleted from electoral rolls.After the meeting, the Lok Sabha LoP said he was surprised that Murmu had not denied the opposition’s allegations of “vote chori” and had instead asked them to provide evidence. “I was shocked that the President did not deny Vote Chori. Instead, she asked us to bring her proof. We will bring her a mountain of it,” he wrote on X.The BJP subsequently attacked Gandhi over his remarks, accusing him of misrepresenting the interaction and dragging the President into a political confrontation. BJP national spokesperson Sambit Patra called the Congress leader a “nalayak neta” and argued that accepting a memorandum did not amount to endorsing its contents.“The anarchist Rahul Gandhi tried to pull the President of India into the anarchism which he's trying his best to conduct on the streets of India,” Patra said.BJP MP Ravi Shankar Prasad also criticised the Opposition’s protests, saying the country would be governed by Parliament, not the streets. “We are not opposed to protests, but you have weaponised street protests because of your electoral defeats,” he said.
Article Summary: Chief Justice of India Surya Kant has rejected the INDIA bloc leaders’ request for a meeting to submit a representation on alleged “vote chori” In an email response to the opposition leaders, the CJI explained the reasons for declining their request. He asked the Congress leader to file a petition on the judicial side.
